assumptions: The count of an area is Poisson around its expected count times its relative risk
Neighbouring areas have similar risks (kind icar, car or bym2), or the areas are independent (kind iid)
An island is linked to the area with the closest border, unless you change the islands setting
The covariate has the same effect in every area
avoid_when: You have the location of each case, not counts for each area (use a point model)
The values are not counts, for example a mean income for each area
You must predict areas that are not on the map (the graph has only the fitted areas)
The data change over time and you want a forecast
data_needs: A count of cases and an expected count (age-standardised) for each area
One covariate for each area, for example a percentage
Which areas are neighbours (an adjacency matrix), for example from shared borders
The outline of each area (polygon points), for the maps and to link islands
about.example: Map lip cancer in the 56 districts of Scotland from 1975 to 1980. Get the smoothed relative risk of each district, find the 19 districts where the risk is surely above the national level, and see the effect of outdoor work fall from 1.96 to 1.5 per 10 points when neighbours share their risk.
about.expert_notes: Poisson(E_i exp(b0 + b1 x_i + u_i)) with x = (covariate - mean) / covariate_scale (pymc-challenges E18). kind: poisson (u = 0), iid (u = sigma theta), icar (sigma pm.ICAR(W), soft sum-to-zero), car (pm.CAR with alpha ~ U(0, 1), tau = 1 / sigma^2; alpha piles up near 1 and b0 mixes slowly) or bym2 (Riebler et al. 2016: u = sigma (sqrt(rho / s) phi + sqrt(1 - rho) theta), s = geometric mean of diag(pinv(D - W)), rho ~ Beta(1, 1)). b0, b1 ~ N(0, 1), sigma ~ HalfNormal(1). islands: link_nearest joins each area without neighbours (then each separate piece) to the area with the closest polygon vertex; isolate keeps them (iid and icar only: an isolated ICAR node has a flat prior); error refuses. The pointwise log-likelihood is always kept, so elpd_loo compares the kinds (Pareto k is often high: one parameter per area). A mask_block split over area holds districts out of the likelihood but keeps them in the graph (leave-areas-out). simulate draws new area effects per draw with a hand-written ICAR sampler (eigenvectors of the Laplacian), as pm.ICAR cannot be forward-sampled. On the Scottish data the AFF effect drops from 0.67 (iid) to about 0.4 (spatial kinds): spatial confounding.
outputs: The smoothed relative risk of each area, with a range
The probability that the relative risk of each area is above 1
The expected cases of each area, and new counts and maps (simulate)
The effect of the covariate, the size of the area effects and the share of them that follows the map (rho, kind bym2)

references.title: Riebler et al. (2016), An intuitive Bayesian spatial model for disease mapping that accounts for scaling
Besag, York and Mollié (1991), Bayesian image restoration, with two applications in spatial statistics
Clayton and Kaldor (1987), Empirical Bayes estimates of age-standardized relative risks for use in disease mapping

about.summary_plain: Estimates the risk of a disease in each area of a map (a district or a county) from small counts, and uses the neighbouring areas to make the estimates of small areas more stable. It also gives the probability that the risk of each area is above the national level.
about.title: Disease risk on a map of areas
use_when: You have counts of cases and expected counts for each area of a map
Some areas are small, so their raw rates are noisy
You want a map of the risk and of the areas where it is surely high
You want to know if a cause (a covariate) explains the map, and how much the answer changes when the areas share their risk with their neighbours

manifest.description: Counts of a disease in areas (districts, counties) against their expected counts, with a covariate and area effects that borrow strength from neighbouring areas: an ICAR, a proper CAR, BYM2 (a scaled ICAR mixed with independent noise) or iid effects. Outputs the smoothed relative risk of each area, the probability that it is above 1, and the expected counts. The polygons and the graph go into the bundle for the maps.

cases.description: Cases in each area: the expected count expected * rr, or a Poisson draw

effect.description: The area effect u on the log relative risk (what the covariate does not explain)

p_exceed.description: 1 when rr is above exceed_threshold in a draw, else 0: the mean over draws is the probability P(rr > threshold)

rr.description: Relative risk of each area (1 = the reference rate)

area.description: The areas (districts, counties): the nodes of the graph

area_.description: The same areas, as the second axis of the adjacency matrix

vertex.description: Vertices of the polygon outlines (NaN padded)

center_covariate.description: Subtract the mean of the covariate
center_covariate.title: Center Covariate

covariate_scale.description: Divide the centred covariate by this (b1 is the effect of one unit)
covariate_scale.title: Covariate Scale

exceed_threshold.description: p_exceed is the probability that rr is above this value
exceed_threshold.title: Exceed Threshold

intercept_sd.description: Prior sd of the intercept b0
intercept_sd.title: Intercept Sd

islands.description: Areas without neighbours: link_nearest links each to the area with the closest boundary; isolate keeps them alone (iid and icar only); error stops (x-ui-level: basic)
islands.title: Islands

kind.description: Prior of the area effects: poisson (none), iid, icar, car (proper CAR) or bym2 (ICAR plus iid with a mixing share rho) (x-ui-level: basic)
kind.title: Kind

rho_alpha.description: Beta prior of rho (bym2): first shape
rho_alpha.title: Rho Alpha

rho_beta.description: Beta prior of rho (bym2): second shape
rho_beta.title: Rho Beta

sigma_scale.description: Half-normal scale of sigma, the sd of the area effects
sigma_scale.title: Sigma Scale

slope_sd.description: Prior sd of the covariate effect b1
slope_sd.title: Slope Sd
